=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text minus "-"
text tri "55 94 48 95 30 96 77 71 26 67 97 13 76 38 45 07 36 79 16 37 68 48 07 09 18 70 26 06 18 72 79 46 59 79 29 90 20 76 87 11 32 07 07 49 18 27 83 58 35 71 11 25 57 29 85 14 64 36 96 27 11 58 56 92 18 55 02 90 03 60 48 49 41 46 33 36 47 23 92 50 48 02 36 59 42 79 72 20 82 77 42 56 78 38 80 39 75 02 71 66 66 01 03 55 72 44 25 67 84 71 67 11 61 40 57 58 89 40 56 36 85 32 25 85 57 48 84 35 47 62 17 01 01 99 89 52 06 71 28 75 94 48 37 10 23 51 06 48 53 18 74 98 15 27 02 92 23 08 71 76 84 15 52 92 63 81 10 44 10 69 93"
text tsmall "55 94 48 95 30 96 77 71 26 67"
text tmax "maximum path sum: "
global vals long 171
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note emiti writes a signed n; the magnitude is taken as a ulong so the minimum long cannot overflow
fn emiti n long to void
if lt n 0
emit minus
emitu add bitcast ulong not n 1
else
emitu ulong n
end
end
note parse reads the decimal numbers in s (separated by spaces, an optional - sign) into vals and
note returns how many; one pass over s, so the loop is bounded by len s
fn parse s view uchar * to ulong
n = ulong 0
v = long 0
sg = long 1
dig = false
for i ulong len s
c = get s i
if eq c 45
sg = long -1
else
if and ge c 48 le c 57
v = add mul v 10 long sub c 48
dig = true
else
if dig
put vals n mul sg v
n = add n 1
end
v = long 0
sg = long 1
dig = false
end
end
end
if dig
put vals n mul sg v
n = add n 1
end
ret n
end
note fold adds to vals[p] the larger of vals[q] and vals[q+1], the two entries below it
fn fold p ulong q ulong to void
lft = get vals q
rgt = get vals add q 1
if gt lft rgt
put vals p add get vals p lft
else
put vals p add get vals p rgt
end
end
note rows are stored one after another, so row r starts at r*(r+1)/2; the sum folds from the bottom row
note up, each entry adding the larger of the two entries below it, until vals[0] holds the answer
fn best rows ulong to long
for x ulong sub rows 1
r = sub sub rows x 2
b = div mul r add r 1 2
nb = add b add r 1
for c ulong add r 1
fold add b c add nb c
end
end
ret get vals 0
end
fn main to int
n = parse tsmall
emit tmax
emiti best 4
emit nl
n = parse tri
emit tmax
emiti best 18
emit nl
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
